senses.definition: (of speech sounds) forming the nucleus of a syllable
examples: the syllabic ‘l’ in ‘riddle’

senses.definition: (of verse) having lines based on number of syllables rather than on rhythmical arrangement of stresses or quantities
consisting of a syllable or syllables
consisting of or using a syllabary
examples: eskimos of the eastern Arctic have a system of syllabic writing

senses.definition: of or relating to syllables
examples: syllabic accent
syllabic characters each represent a syllable

senses.definition: a unit of spoken language larger than a phoneme
examples: the word ‘pocket’ has two syllables

senses.definition: an arbitrary sign (written or printed) that has acquired a conventional significance
something visible that by association or convention represents something else that is invisible
examples: the eagle is a symbol of the United States

senses.definition: relating to or using or proceeding by means of symbols
examples: symbolic logic
symbolic operations
symbolic thinking

senses.definition: serving as a visible symbol for something abstract
examples: a crown is emblematic of royalty
the spinning wheel was as symbolic of colonical Massachusetts as the codfish

senses.definition: using symbolism
examples: symbolic art

senses.definition: (of characters in literature or drama) evoking empathic or sympathetic feelings
examples: the sympathetic characters in the play

senses.definition: expressing or feeling or resulting from sympathy or compassion or friendly fellow feelings; disposed toward
examples: sympathetic to the students' cause
a sympathetic observer
a sympathetic gesture

senses.definition: having similar disposition and tastes
examples: with their many similar tastes, he found her a most sympathetic companion

senses.definition: of or relating to the sympathetic nervous system
examples: sympathetic neurons
sympathetic stimulation

senses.definition: relating to vibrations that occur as a result of vibrations in a nearby body
examples: sympathetic vibration

senses.definition: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
examples: was charitable in his opinions of others
kindly criticism
a kindly act
sympathetic words
a large-hearted mentor

senses.definition: a relation of affinity or harmony between people; whatever affects one correspondingly affects the other
examples: the two of them were in close sympathy

senses.definition: an inclination to support or be loyal to or to agree with an opinion
examples: his sympathies were always with the underdog
I knew I could count on his understanding

senses.definition: sharing the feelings of others (especially feelings of sorrow or anguish)
a large orchestra; can perform symphonies
examples: we heard the Vienna symphony

senses.definition: a long and complex sonata for symphony orchestra
(medicine) any sensation or change in bodily function that is experienced by a patient and is associated with a particular disease
anything that accompanies X and is regarded as an indication of X's existence
characteristic or indicative of a disease
examples: a diagnostic sign of yellow fever
a rash symptomatic of scarlet fever
symptomatic of insanity
a rise in crime symptomatic of social breakdown

senses.definition: relating to or according to or affecting a symptom or symptoms
examples: symptomatic relief
symptomatic treatment
a symptomatic classification of diseases

senses.definition: a complex of concurrent things
examples: every word has a syndrome of meanings

senses.definition: a pattern of symptoms indicative of some disease
two words that can be interchanged in a context are said to be synonymous relative to that context
a sketchy summary of the main points of an argument or theory
reasoning from the general to the particular (or from cause to effect)
the combination of ideas into a complex whole
the process of producing a chemical compound (usually by the union of simpler chemical compounds)
artificial as if portrayed in a film
examples: a novel with flat celluloid characters

senses.definition: involving or of the nature of synthesis (combining separate elements to form a coherent whole) as opposed to analysis
examples: limnology is essentially a synthetic science composed of elements … that extend well beyond the limits of biology

senses.definition: not genuine or natural
examples: counterfeit rhetoric that flourishes when passions are synthetic

senses.definition: not of natural origin; prepared or made artificially
examples: man-made fibers
synthetic leather

senses.definition: of a proposition whose truth value is determined by observation or facts
examples: ‘all men are arrogant’ is a synthetic proposition

senses.definition: systematic combining of root and modifying elements into single words
a compound made artificially by chemical reactions
by synthesis; in a synthetic manner
examples: some of these drugs have been derived from opium and others have been produced synthetically

senses.definition: (physical chemistry) a sample of matter in which substances in different phases are in equilibrium
examples: in a static system, oil cannot be replaced by water on a surface
a system generating hydrogen peroxide

senses.definition: a complex of methods or rules governing behavior
examples: they have to operate under a system they oppose
that language has a complex system for indicating gender

senses.definition: a group of independent but interrelated elements comprising a unified whole
examples: a vast system of production and distribution and consumption keep the country going

senses.definition: a group of physiologically or anatomically related organs or parts
examples: the body has a system of organs for digestion

senses.definition: a procedure or process for obtaining an objective
examples: they had to devise a system that did not depend on cooperation

senses.definition: an ordered manner; orderliness by virtue of being methodical and well organized
examples: his compulsive organization was not an endearing quality
we can't do it unless we establish some system around here

senses.definition: an organized structure for arranging or classifying
examples: he changed the arrangement of the topics
the facts were familiar but it was in the organization of them that he was original
he tried to understand their system of classification

senses.definition: instrumentality that combines interrelated interacting artifacts designed to work as a coherent entity
examples: he bought a new stereo system
the system consists of a motor and a small computer

senses.definition: the living body considered as made up of interdependent components forming a unified whole
examples: exercise helped him get the alcohol out of his system

senses.definition: characterized by order and planning
examples: the investigation was very systematic
a systematic administrator

senses.definition: of or relating to taxonomy
examples: taxonomic relations
a taxonomic designation
